title: Multitask neural screening identifies compounds active against Leishmania infantum in vitro
summary: Multitask neural classification and regression screened approximately 1.3 million purchasable compounds for Leishmania infantum activity. After physicochemical and human structural filtering, 20 selected compounds were tested; nine inhibited promastigotes in vitro. Three had more favorable source-reported selectivity, with LC-15 showing an IC50 of 1.05 µM and selectivity index 30.9. LC-15 was already disclosed in a 2023 antitrypanosomal study; this entry represents the Leishmania result, not a new chemical entity. Intracellular parasite activity, animal efficacy and a proposed proteasome mechanism were not established.
ai_technology: Multitask deep neural network classification and regression; molecular fingerprints
organization: Federal University of Goiás; University of Brasília

evidence.tested: Twenty model-prioritized, subsequently filtered compounds were evaluated against Leishmania infantum promastigotes. Nine were active; cytotoxicity and selectivity measurements were reported for selected active hits. Three had source-described selectivity indices above 9.
evidence.unknown: No intracellular-amastigote efficacy, animal therapeutic efficacy or clinical benefit is established. Six active compounds had less favorable selectivity. LC-15 is the same chemical entity disclosed in the 2023 antitrypanosomal study, whose supplement also reports the same MRC-5 cytotoxicity value; independently new cytotoxicity evidence is not inferred. Its proteasome mechanism remains a hypothesis, and the observed hit rate is not a controlled comparison with conventional screening.
evidence.ai_role: Multitask DNN classifiers and regressors transferred information across three Leishmania species to prioritize untested molecules; physicochemical filters, similarity analysis and human inspection then selected 20 for experiments.

source_review.scope: Corrected exact primary DOI/title/PMCID and electronic date; full computational prioritization and result-specific activity/selectivity paragraphs; current PubMed publication-status relationships. Earlier metadata lookup had retrieved a different paper and is not used as evidence. Compared the original 2023 and 2024 author supplements by exact LC-15 chemical name, structure, supplier identifier and NMR evidence; the represented novelty is the Leishmania assay, not chemical-entity novelty.
